key_insight: Kirigami parachutes can be designed for strong drag and stable inverted flight when the deployment height is about one parachute radius, but smaller deployments become dynamically unstable and tumble.
engineering_relevance: The paper gives a simple geometric design rule for deployable parachutes: target deployment heights near the radius to balance high drag with robust flight stability.
method: Simulated prescribed-acceleration and free-fall dynamics of a parameterized kirigami parachute.
Used a novel Biot-Savart far-field boundary condition to mimic effectively infinite domains.
Reconstructed far-field velocity from interior vorticity to reduce boundary effects.
evidence_signal: The far-field treatment changed predicted dynamics by less than 0.1% when the domain size was doubled, and the study reports 2-5x drops in linear forces during deployment alongside increased moments and stability measurements across deployment heights.
watch_item: The stability rule is derived from numerical simulations of a parameterized geometry, so performance may shift with different materials, Reynolds numbers, or real-world deployment conditions.
paper_title: Stability of Kirigami parachutes in effectively infinite numerical domains
